children.text: Participants
ThinkByte: Revanth Babu Raavi, Harsha Thota
Sigmainfo: Sonam Dahake, Sandeep Phophaliya, to: Shiresha Madhury, Divya Mishra, Magesh R
Key Takeaways
Discussion clarified that the target traffic metric (715) should be mapped to column D in Google Analytics, emphasizing organic search as the primary data source.
The plugin update for the Big Index Now tool is scheduled to be addressed, with plans to install or update it by tomorrow.
A decision was made to implement a new URL structure for Sigma’s website using the services folder approach, ensuring SEO-friendly and structured navigation.
It was highlighted that a significant drop in conversion rates—from a baseline of 3-4% to about 1.7%—warrants daily monitoring and the establishment of automated triggers using inspection tools.
A refined keyword research strategy for Lendfoundry was proposed, focusing on building diverse topic clusters (e.g., application intake) to drive more tailored content creation.
Action Items
Noted that while blog content was being managed, service pages were often neglected and not updated.

Share the keyword research and topics sheet link in the WhatsApp group for team access.
Add the agreed action items for daily form conversion tracking and service page optimization to the meeting minutes (MoM).

Harsha Thota
Monitor for repeated junk lead submissions from the same IP address and, if excessive, arrange to block those IPs.
Set up a daily monitoring trigger for form conversion tracking on the website and coordinate with Shiresha to establish an alert mechanism.
Conduct a complete analysis using Inspectlet (or a comparable tool) to identify issues affecting form submissions, and report findings.
Identify and track performance of selected high‐intent service pages on the Lendfoundry website, and coordinate a plan to improve their rankings and lead conversions.

Provide the available log file data for Lendfoundry, preferably covering up to 30 days, and share it with the team.
Current Workflow
Team monitors organic traffic and leads using Google Analytics, Search Console, and weekly metrics tracker sheets, supported by log file analyses.
Pain Points
Lendfoundry is receiving numerous junk submissions (e.g., irrelevant data vendor queries) affecting lead quality.
Inefficiencies Observed
Complex, multi-directory URL structures were debated, with concerns that excessive directories add unnecessary complexity.
No automated daily trigger exists to detect form malfunctions, leading to delayed response on conversion drops.
Key Stakeholders
Sandeep Phophaliya emphasizes the need for process improvements and daily performance monitoring.
Revanth Babu Raavi and Magesh R are responsible for implementing URL structure changes, plugin installations, and handling hosting-related technicalities.
Harsha Thota is tasked with rechecking conversion metrics and coordinating improvements on form functionality and service page tracking.
Tools / Systems Used
Systems include Google Analytics, Google Search Console, and Wordpress (with contact form plugins), with log file analysis performed on Cloudways and AWS.
User session tracking tools like Inspectlet/Clarity are considered to diagnose form issues and user experience.
Root Causes Identified
Unfiltered submissions from specific IP addresses contribute to junk leads that are not effectively blocked.
Suspected form malfunction, possibly due to expired recaptcha or technical glitches, is causing lower lead submissions.
Proposed Improvements
Install the Big Index plugin by tomorrow to enhance site indexing; Magesh R to action this.
Adopt a simplified URL structure based on a 'services' pattern to reduce directory complexity and improve SEO crawl efficiency.
Set up a daily monitoring process (potentially via bot tests) to trigger alerts when form fills drop unexpectedly.
Develop targeted keyword clusters for application intake and service pages to diversify blog content and boost ranking.
Pilot the tracking and optimization process on selected Land Foundry service pages to improve high-intent lead performance.
Impact
Expected improvements include higher lead conversion rates, improved SEO crawl/indexing due to better URL structure, and timely detection and mitigation of form issues.
Metrics
Approximately 80% of submissions are from job seekers, with a focus on increasing qualified leads (MQLs) and reducing irrelevant inquiries.
Target traffic for the month was set at 715, while actual weekly traffic figures varied (e.g., 572, 511, 340), and lead conversion rates fell from 3-4% to 1.7%.
Risk
Complex URL structures, if not simplified, may continue to hinder effective SEO and negatively impact organic traffic rankings.
Ongoing form malfunctions risk further drop in qualified lead capture if not swiftly detected and resolved.
Lead Quality Assessment

Both Sigma and Lendfoundry are receiving predominantly job seeker and irrelevant inquiries (e.g., data vendor queries), with no real marketing qualified leads, prompting plans to filter junk leads if the volume increases.
URL Structure Strategy

The team agreed to adopt a streamlined URL structure that uses a single parent 'services' folder for ecommerce pages (e.g., sigmainfo.net/aim/ecommerce/developmentservices) to improve SEO and crawlability.
Performance Metrics Review

Sigma’s conversion rate dropped from a baseline of 3-4% to 1.7% despite steady traffic, and Lendfoundry saw a decline in both traffic (from 572 to 349) and leads (from 24 to 13) over successive weeks.
Form Functionality Analysis

A potential issue with form performance was identified due to the drop in lead conversion; the team plans to set up a daily monitor (using a bot or inspector tool) to trigger alerts if the form fails or underperforms.
Content Strategy Development

A diversified content strategy is required for Lendfoundry, including the creation of keyword clusters and topics around subpages like application intake to break the current content rut and target both LOS and API-based queries.
